explanation: Commit `967b418eef381bb97d80494904c44e8ada806024` changed search from an inverted-index lookup to a per-request full scan of `CATALOG`. In `searchProducts()`, the call switched from `matchPositions(POSTINGS, tokens)` to `matchPositions(CATALOG, tokens)`, and `matchPositions()` stopped intersecting postings lists and instead normalized every product, split it into words, then for every query token checked both substring matches and a Levenshtein-distance fallback against every word. That moved work from a small precomputed index into nested request-time loops over all products and words, making each search O(products * words * token comparisons * edit-distance cost)` instead of mostly touching only matching postings.
suggestedFix: Keep fuzzy/partial matching, but move candidate generation back onto an index. I would restore the postings-list path for exact tokens and add a separate token dictionary or n-gram/prefix index to expand each query token into a bounded candidate set before scoring, only running edit-distance checks on those candidates. That preserves the typo-tolerance feature, but costs some extra memory at startup and a more complex index build path.
culpritSubject: fix: match partial words and common misspellings in search

$scarn_notifications_v1.body: `git bisect run` isolated commit `967b418eef381bb97d80494904c44e8ada806024` (`fix: match partial words and common misspellings in search`) as the first revision where GET /api/search crossed the 5.24ms p95 threshold. Parent commit p95 was 0.549ms; culprit commit p95 was 60.827ms.
$scarn_notifications_v1.title: Search regression culprit identified
